title: Consent-aware streaming redact gateway + manifest-driven erase workflow for console telemetry
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Replace ad-hoc batch scrubbing for console telemetry with a streaming redact gateway that enforces per-customer retention and consent rules at ingest, emits immutable deletion manifests, and coordinates downstream erasure across analytics, observability, and exports. This ticket builds the gateway, the manifest spec and signer, the Erase Orchestrator consumer, and the rollout plan with canary and audit trails.

Motivation: Current pipeline performs offline PII redaction during nightly jobs which causes long windows where raw identifiers exist in intermediate stores (kafka topics / staging tables). We need a streaming-first approach to minimize retention surface, make deletion provable, and enable fast compliance for legal requests and customer-initiated erasures.

High-level design:
- Redact Gateway (Kubernetes service fronting ingestion): applies attribute-level rules, deterministic pseudonymization (per-tenant keyed hash) for non-reversible pseudomaps, and optional tokenization for erasable mappings stored in the KV Gateway with limited TTL.
- Consent & Retention Engine (policy service): evaluates customer consent flags, legal holds, and product-level retention windows to decide redaction vs keep vs escrowed-token flows.
- Deletion Manifest Spec: compact JSON lines manifest listing affected topics/tables, partition ranges, sequence numbers, pseudomap tokens to expire, and an RFC-3339 timestamp for requested deletion. Manifests are signed by the gateway and published to a high-availability manifest topic.
- Erase Orchestrator (consumer): subscribes to manifests, coordinates idempotent erasures across sinks (bigquery, clickhouse, s3 telemetry archives, internal visibility services), ensures transactional progress via checkpoints, and emits attestation events to the audit log.
- Backfill & Repair: a bounded backfill path to handle historical rows that were ingested before the gateway rollout using a manifest-driven scan + rewrite approach.

Acceptance criteria:
- Redact Gateway running in prod-like staging applying per-tenant retention rules to test tenants.
- Manifest spec documented and signed manifests verifiable with public key in our KMS.
- Erase Orchestrator can process a manifest and produce attestations; full pipeline deletions for test manifests complete within SLO.
- End-to-end integration tests (unit + integration) and a canary plan for a small subset of customers.
- Observability: dashboards showing redact rate, manifests emitted, manifest processing latency, and failures with runbook links.

Links and artifacts: Confluence: https://confluence.internal/redwood/console/consent-streaming-redact-gateway (design + schema) ; RFC: https://docs.internal/redwood/rfcs/2026-02-consent-redact-manifests ; Spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4892 ; Prototype Dataflow job: https://grafana.internal/d/streaming-pipeline/ingest-health ; Attestation schema: https://drive.internal/redwood/privacy/attestation-v1.json
acceptance_criteria: Gateway applies per-tenant retention and consent rules at ingest
Signed deletion manifests published to manifest topic
Erase Orchestrator performs idempotent erase and emits attestations
Integration tests for backfill and live ingest pass
Dashboards and alerting covering manifest failures and processing lag
updates: 2026-02-22: Kickoff meeting with PM and Legal. Agreed manifest must include partition ranges and expirable token ids.
2026-03-01: Prototype gateway implemented for JSON events; deterministic pseudomap using tenant-scoped HMAC performed at ~8k events/s on t3-medium equivalent. Spike PR opened (PR #4892).

2026-03-05: Performance concerns: current pseudomap writes to KV Gateway at ingest increases P99 latency ~45ms. Decided to default to deterministic hash for most attributes and only token-store for sensitive identifiers behind feature flag.
2026-03-08: Legal requested additional field 'legal_hold_reason' in manifest and approval to retain manifests for 365 days in audit-store. Updated spec draft.

2026-03-12: Erase Orchestrator PoC can replay manifests against test ClickHouse sink; observed retry storm causing DB connection exhaustion—throttling added and coordinator now uses bounded concurrency.
2026-03-14: Security review kickoff scheduled; Samir to prepare threat model and KMS key rotation plan. Planning canary rollout to 5 internal tenants in 2026-W12.
